newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian industry urges tax breaks for investment.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian industry urges tax breaks for investment.

text.p: The Bulgarian Industry Union (BIU) urged authorities to boost declining production through customs duty and tax breaks in a draft bill submitted to parliament for approval, BIU chairman said.
"We have proposed to parliament to lift customs duties on imported technologies and equipment and reduce or abolish corporate tax on investment," BIU chairman Krastyo Stanilov said.
Corporate tax in Bulgaria is 26 percent for a profit of up to two million levs and 36 percent for a profit over that amount.
Pending introduction of a restrictive monetary regime in July and steps to speed up privatisation were not enough to increase investor interest, id Stanilov.

The new reformist Bulgarian cabinet which took office on May 21 pledged to speed up structural reform and introduce a fixed rate exchange regime called a currency board system to stabilise the economy and the fragile lev currency.
The BIU was set up in 1990 by Bulgarian private and state industrial firms.
Bulgarian year-on-year industrial output fell a real 15.4 percent in the first quarter of 1997 due to the shrinking demand, soaring inflation and the sharp lev fall against the dollar.

Political instability and delayed reforms pushed first quarter cumulative consumer price inflation to 452 percent and March inflation was 2,040.5 percent. Producer prices rose 2,072.7 percent year on year in March. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
